title: A Uniform for the Bridge
premise: In 1747 Marseille, Elodie Delacroix, apprentice to a dead mapmaker, is secretly completing the atlas of the harbor fortifications that cost her master his life. When an orphaned child arrives at their door clutching a coded drawing that matches the atlas's missing final plate, Elodie realizes the two documents together could condemn—or save—the families living along the seawall slated for demolition. Smuggling both past three military checkpoints, Elodie finds unexpected allies among dockworkers, nuns, and a conflicted officer, and learns that invisibility was always an illusion. In the end, Elode surrenders the atlas to the Crown but keeps the child, choosing found family over the map's legacy.
about_author: D. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing eighteenth-century port records in southern France. Their fiction blends meticulous historical detail with intimate stories of people history forgot to name.

chapters.title: The Ink That Outlived Him
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Working alone at night, Elodie inks the dead master's coastlines and hides the unfinished atlas beneath floorboards. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into quiet purpose, and the fear of being caught with dangerous paper.

chapters.title: A Bundle at the Door
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A six-year-old boy, Tomas, is left on the doorstep with a note: forget the face. He clutches a coded drawing Elodie half-recognizes. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility cracking open a carefully closed life.

chapters.title: What the Child Carried
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Comparing Tomas's drawing to the master's notes, Elodie discovers it is the missing final plate—the seawall survey the master died protecting. Emotional beat: dread and awe as the atlas becomes truly lethal knowledge.

chapters.title: The Widow Couteau
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV, filtered through Elodie's observation. The neighbor widow feeds the boy and asks no questions, revealing she once hid fugitives too. Emotional beat: first hint that Elodie's solitude was never as complete as believed.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Disguising the plates inside a delivery of vellum, Elodie passes the first checkpoint by flattering a bored clerk—but a soldier notes their face. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by the cost of being seen.

chapters.title: Lieutenant Roche
chapters.summary: Roche's POV. The young officer assigned to find the missing survey recognizes the master's hand from his academy days and begins to doubt his orders. Emotional beat: duty straining against conscience.

chapters.title: The Nuns of Saint-Victor
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Seeking temporary shelter for Tomas, Elodie bargains with Mother Anselme, who agrees only if Elodie admits why the boy matters. Emotional beat: confession as the price of help; found family taking root.

chapters.title: The Demolition Order
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs via overheard proclamation. The Crown announces the seawall quarter will be razed within the month. Emotional beat: the abstract map becomes imminent, human catastrophe.

chapters.title: Dockworkers' Ledger
chapters.summary: Baptiste, a stevedore, narrates. He offers smugglers' routes through the harbor in exchange for copies of the survey proving his home stands on solid ground, not the claimed marsh. Emotional beat: solidarity forged from shared stakes.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Gate of the Arsenal
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. A search nearly exposes the plates hidden in Tomas's toy boat; Roche arrives and, deliberately misreading the manifest, waves them through. Emotional beat: gratitude entangled with suspicion—why did he lie?

chapters.title: The Master's Letters
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Deciphering the master's correspondence, Elodie learns he had a daughter—and that Tomas may be her son, his grandchild. Emotional beat: the found family revealed as blood family, love deepening into inheritance.

chapters.title: Roche's Doubt
chapters.summary: Roche's POV. Ordered to raid the convent, Roche stalls, forging paperwork to buy time. Emotional beat: the moment duty tips toward betrayal of the uniform he wears.

chapters.title: The Raid That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Soldiers sweep Saint-Victor while Elodie hides in the crypt with Tomas among the bones. Emotional beat: terror transformed into fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Harbor Watch
chapters.summary: Baptiste's POV. The plates move by fishing boat, but the harbor watch seizes the vessel. Emotional beat: the plan collapsing, allies scattered, hope gutted.

chapters.title: What Baptiste Paid
chapters.summary: Baptiste's POV. Interrogated, Baptiste gives nothing away despite a broken hand. Emotional beat: sacrifice proving the found family is real, not convenient.

chapters.title: The Face They Were Told to Forget
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Tracing the note's seal, Elodie identifies the woman who left Tomas: the master's daughter, alive, hiding from the same men. Emotional beat: fury and longing colliding—abandonment reframed as protection.

chapters.title: Roche's Choice
chapters.summary: Roche's POV. Confronted with proof his superiors falsified the seawall reports, Roche must decide between promotion and truth. Emotional beat: the climax of conscience—he chooses the atlas over the uniform.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints, One Night
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Elodie, Roche, and Baptiste run the evidence through all three checkpoints in a single coordinated night as the demolition crews mobilize. Emotional beat: breathless unity, every ally risking everything at once.

chapters.title: The Atlas Before the Council
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The completed atlas and the coded plate are presented to the royal council, exposing the falsified surveys. Emotional beat: vindication laced with fear—truth spoken to power for the master's sake.

chapters.title: What the Crown Keeps
chapters.summary: Roche's POV. The Crown confiscates the atlas but halts the demolitions; Roche resigns rather than serve the men who lied. Emotional beat: bittersweet victory—justice partial, integrity intact.

chapters.title: The Daughter Returns
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The master's daughter comes for Tomas, then chooses to stay, mending what abandonment broke. Emotional beat: forgiveness without erasure; grief finally given somewhere to rest.

chapters.title: A Uniform for the Bridge
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, epilogue. A year later, Elodie draws new maps—not of fortifications but of homes—and hangs Roche's discarded uniform coat by the door as a reminder. Emotional beat: peace earned; memory, love, and family outlasting every border drawn.
